messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: high GPU memory fragmentation + continuous-batching spike on kv-cache on host-pool-gpu-7. Error rate climbing, tail latency > 2s for emb endpoint. Alert: kv_cache_fragmentation > 0.25 and contbatch_queue_depth > 200
jen: acked, I'm oncall. grabbing logs now. tagging infra-jen for arena knobs.
jen: quick context: this started after the 03:12 canary deploy of batching heuristics (contbatch-policy=v2). We see a gradual growth in slab fragmentation and repeated smaller allocations failing, leading to backpressure.
tony: seeing same in telemetry. heatmap of active slabs showing many tiny free ranges. suspect allocator reslice churn with small token sizes.
maria: customer-ops reports elevated latency for 3 mid-market customers on embeddings. they're seeing timeouts for long prompts. raising priority.
ajay: do we have a safe rollback of contbatch-policy? can we flip to v1?
jen: yes, plan: 1) flip contbatch-policy -> v1 (immediate) 2) apply temporary batch_size cap 3) trigger per-host process restart if mem > 85% 4) run compaction/arena-reslice patch on affected hosts (non-blocking)
sarah: pushing the rollback now. running: 
```
# disable new contbatch heuristic
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  https://console.internal.redwood/api/v1/configs/contbatch -d '{"policy":"v1"}'
```
sarah: rollback accepted by control plane. new config is propagating to pool. :white_check_mark:
metrics-bot: config_event: contbatch.policy change v2->v1 by sarah at 3924512379
jen: while that propagates, set per-host throttles to avoid eviction storms. running one-off script to set batch_size_max=128 on pool.
ajay: I'm preparing a hotfix patch to avoid allocator reslice thrash: set arena_reslice_threshold to 64KB and enable eager_compact=true. will roll to canary 2 hosts first.
tony: logs from host-pool-gpu-7: 
```
E Allocation failed: cudaMalloc 134217728 returned OOM at python3:torch
W KV slab fragmentation > 0.30 mid-queue
I Dropping request after retry window exceeded
```
maria: customer-ops: I've let the customers know we see a degradation and we're rolling a targeted fix. offered ETA ~20-30m. they're asking if tokens are lost or data impacted.
jen: customers unaffected for data integrity; only latency/timeouts. we should add a short note to status page.
jen: can someone run safe compaction on 7 and 9? command: `sudo /opt/redwood/bin/arena-compact --safe` (non-disruptive, but CPU heavy).
ajay: starting canary compaction on gpu-9 now. will monitor mem and tail latency.
sarah: compaction kicked off on gpu-9. current mem drop -3% after first pass.
metrics-bot: alert suppressed: kv_cache_fragmentation now 0.19 on gpu-9 after compaction
jen: good. continue. sarah, after canary verify, roll to rest of affected hosts. also keep contbatch-policy at v1 until we analyze regression.
tony: pushing script to restart workers gracefully when mem > 85% and after compaction completes. script attached: 
```
for host in $(cat affected_hosts); do
  ssh $host 'systemctl restart redwood-worker --no-block'
done
```
maria: customers updated. one asked for a SLA credit estimate; escalate to sales if needed.
customer-ops: noted. will collect impacted request ids and attach to ticket.
jen: postmortem actions (short): 1) revert contbatch v2 until regression root cause understood 2) add safety cap to batch size in v2 3) instrument per-slab fragmentation metrics 4) add automatic compaction trigger when fragmentation > 0.22 5) run allocator stress test in preprod with contbatch v2
ajay: opening PR for allocator knobs and a non-urgent CI stress job. will link in thread.
jen: handoff to night oncall @tony in 30m. all immediate mitigations applied. last checks before handoff.
ton y: ack, taking over. I'll keep the rollback in place and monitor. ping me if any customer escalates. :thumbsup:
jen: thanks team. closing pager after an hour of stable metrics. leaving instructions in the runbook channel and will follow up with a proper incident page.
incident-bot: Incident update: state=stabilized, severity=high -> monitoring. pager resolved at 3924514820
